title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
keyIdea: Cut at mid and one half is always sorted (the array drops only once). nums[low] <= nums[mid] → left half sorted, else right half. If target lies between the sorted half's two ends, search that half; otherwise search the other half.

approaches.name: Scan everything
approaches.why: Correct, but the problem asks for O(log n).

approaches.name: Find the pivot, then binary search one part
approaches.idea: Find the minimum's index like LC 153. Both sides of it are sorted: if nums[pivot] <= target <= nums[n − 1] search pivot…n−1, else 0…pivot−1.
approaches.why: Two binary searches, log n each. Easier to reason about, a bit more code.

approaches.name: One pass: check the sorted half
approaches.idea: mid == target → done. nums[low] <= nums[mid] → left sorted: target in [nums[low], nums[mid]] → high = mid − 1, else low = mid + 1. Otherwise right sorted: target in [nums[mid], nums[high]] → low = mid + 1, else high = mid − 1.
approaches.why: One binary search; each step throws away half.

quiz.q: Why is at least one half always sorted?
options: The array drops only once, so the drop is on one side of mid and the other side has none

quiz.q: Left half is sorted but target is NOT between nums[low] and nums[mid]. What next?
options: low = mid + 1: it can only be in the right half

quiz.q: Why check the range only in the sorted half?
options: Only in a sorted range does 'between its ends' prove target is inside; the other half may wrap around
When low == mid the left half is one element, which is sorted
